acceptance.given: An acceptance-passed publication attempt identifies an actor and the current Acceptance lifecycle owner.

oracle.expected: Derived replay, seed, matrix, review, and Quick Dev evidence exposes authorizes=[]; only an attempt by the current Acceptance lifecycle owner is authorized to publish acceptance-passed, and every other actor is rejected.
forbidden: Publication succeeds without verifying that the actor is the current Acceptance lifecycle owner
oracle.observable: The Toolchain authorization validation records empty authorization sets for derived evidence and an authorization decision for each attempted acceptance-passed publication.

acceptance.then: Acceptance-passed publication is restricted to the current Acceptance lifecycle owner.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain authorization validation evaluates derived evidence and an actor's attempt to publish acceptance-passed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a non-owner acceptance-passed publication attempt and require the authorization validator to reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain finalization verify the current Acceptance lifecycle owner before publishing acceptance-passed, while derived replay, seed, matrix, review, and Quick Dev artifacts retain authorizes=[].

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema compatibility change; rollback restores the prior finalization authorization behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: An acceptance-passed publication attempt is evaluated against the current Acceptance lifecycle owner and becomes authorized or rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authorization validation confirms authorizes=[] for derived evidence, authorizes the current lifecycle owner alone, and rejects every non-owner publication attempt.

acceptance.given: The complete current Consumer Manifest and the in-scope repository real-call surface for VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing are available for reconciliation.

oracle.expected: Bidirectional reconciliation establishes both that every applicable Consumer Manifest entry maps to repository callers and that every in-scope repository caller in VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing has a corresponding Consumer Manifest entry.
forbidden: Any repository caller in VDD, Acceptance, or workflow-model-routing is absent from the Consumer Manifest.
Reconciliation is one-way or omits repository callers from the reverse check.
oracle.observable: The Toolchain reconciliation result reports complete current Consumer Manifest coverage in both directions against the repository real-call surface.

acceptance.then: Every in-scope repository caller is represented in the complete current Consumer Manifest and every applicable manifest Consumer is reconciled to the real-call surface.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain semantic reconciliation validates the complete current Consumer Manifest against repository callers.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a VDD, Acceptance, or workflow-model-routing repository caller missing from the Consumer Manifest and require bidirectional reconciliation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend Toolchain Consumer Manifest reconciliation to inspect the repository real-call surface bidirectionally, covering VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing callers rather than only route reachability or omitted-caller checks.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema compatibility change; rollback restores the prior reconciliation implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: The complete current Consumer Manifest and repository real-call surface move from unreconciled to a bidirectionally checked coverage result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The reconciliation check verifies both manifest-to-caller and caller-to-manifest coverage across VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing, and fails for a missing mapping.

acceptance.given: Historical tracked content exists before repair and its pre-repair byte baseline is available to the Toolchain validation.

oracle.expected: The before-and-after comparison is byte-for-byte identical for every historical tracked artifact during and after repair.
forbidden: Any historical bytes are modified, rewritten, or corrupted by the repair.
oracle.observable: A Toolchain historical-content integrity comparison, evaluated after repair, reports no byte differences from the pre-repair baseline.

acceptance.then: Historical bytes remain identical to their pre-repair state.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain integrity validation compares historical content before and after repair.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a historical tracked artifact with a changed byte and require the integrity comparison to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain repair validation compare frozen historical artifact bytes with post-repair bytes and reject every difference.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema compatibility change; rollback restores the prior historical-byte validation implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Historical content remains at its pre-repair byte baseline after repair validation completes.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The post-repair integrity check reports byte equality for the historical tracked content and rejects every byte mutation.

acceptance.given: Existing repair evidence is present before a new repair evidence record is created.

oracle.expected: New repair evidence is appended after the existing evidence while every pre-existing entry remains unchanged and in its original order.
forbidden: Existing repair evidence is overwritten, edited, deleted, or reordered.
oracle.observable: A Toolchain append-only evidence check, evaluated when recording repair evidence, compares the prior sequence with the resulting sequence and reports the prior sequence unchanged as a prefix.

acceptance.then: Repair evidence consists of the unchanged historical record followed only by newly appended entries.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain records repair evidence and evaluates the append-only evidence boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a repair-evidence result that changes, deletes, overwrites, or reorders a pre-existing entry and require the append-only check to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain repair-evidence recording and validation enforce append-only sequencing: preserve the existing record unchanged and append new evidence after it.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema compatibility change; rollback restores the prior evidence-recording implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: A repair-evidence record changes only by appending new entries after an unchanged existing sequence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The append-only boundary check confirms that the prior evidence sequence is unchanged and ordered before every new entry, and rejects overwrite, edit, deletion, or reordering.
